title: Exact coproduct-preserving functors preserve telescopes
statement:
Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal T'$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with countable coproducts (colimits of discrete diagrams indexed by $\mathbf N$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]). Let $F:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T'$ be an exact functor, with shift isomorphism $\xi_X:F(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X)[1]$, preserving countable coproducts. Let $(E_N,u_N:E_N\to E_{N+1})_{N\in\mathbf N}$ be a sequence. Put $B=\bigoplus_NE_N$, $B'=\bigoplus_NF(E_N)$, with coprojections $\iota_N,\iota'_N$, and define $s\iota_N=\iota_{N+1}u_N$ and $s'\iota'_N=\iota'_{N+1}F(u_N)$. Choose telescope triangles [def-kun-truncations]
$$B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\xrightarrow{p}H\xrightarrow{q}B[1],\qquad B'\xrightarrow{1-s'}B'\xrightarrow{p'}H'\xrightarrow{q'}B'[1].$$
The coproduct comparison $\alpha:B'\to F(B)$ defined by $\alpha\iota'_N=F(\iota_N)$ is an isomorphism. There exists a morphism $c:H'\to F(H)$ satisfying
$$c p'=F(p)\alpha,\qquad \xi_B F(q)c=\alpha[1]q',$$
so that $(\alpha,\alpha,c)$ is a morphism from the telescope triangle for $(F(E_N),F(u_N))$ to the image under $F$ of the telescope triangle for $(E_N,u_N)$. Every such $c$ is an isomorphism. In particular $F(H)$ is a homotopy colimit of $(F(E_N),F(u_N))$; the comparison is relative to these chosen triangles and need not be unique.

proof.text: Use the telescope definition [def-kun-truncations] to fix $B,\iota_N,s,p,q,H$ and the corresponding primed data. The countable coproducts exist by hypothesis, and TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] supplies distinguished cone triangles for $1-s$ and $1-s'$. Thus arbitrary choices of the two telescope triangles in the statement are legitimate.

Apply the universal property of a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] to the discrete $\mathbf N$-diagram to obtain the unique $\alpha:B'\to F(B)$ with $\alpha\iota'_N=F(\iota_N)$. Since $F$ preserves this coproduct, $(F(B),F(\iota_N))$ is also a coproduct cocone. Its universal property gives $\beta:F(B)\to B'$ with $\beta F(\iota_N)=\iota'_N$. The composites $\beta\alpha$ and $\alpha\beta$ restrict to identities on every coprojection, so uniqueness in the two universal properties gives $\beta\alpha=1$ and $\alpha\beta=1$. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), applied to the discrete category on the small set of natural numbers

proof.text:
Check the first square on each coprojection, using the shift-endomorphism formulas of [def-kun-truncations]:
$$\alpha s'\iota'_N=\alpha\iota'_{N+1}F(u_N)=F(\iota_{N+1})F(u_N)=F(\iota_{N+1}u_N)=F(s\iota_N)=F(s)\alpha\iota'_N.$$
The coproduct universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore gives $\alpha s'=F(s)\alpha$. Exactness includes additivity by [def-weil-triangulated-category], so $F(1-s)=1-F(s)$ and subtracting the displayed equality from $\alpha=\alpha$ gives $\alpha(1-s')=F(1-s)\alpha$.

Exactness as defined in [def-weil-triangulated-category] makes
$$F(B)\xrightarrow{F(1-s)}F(B)\xrightarrow{F(p)}F(H)\xrightarrow{\xi_B F(q)}F(B)[1]$$
a distinguished triangle. Step 3 supplies its commuting first square with the primed telescope triangle. Apply TR3 of the same definition to the pair $(\alpha,\alpha)$ to obtain $c:H'\to F(H)$ with $c p'=F(p)\alpha$ and $\xi_B F(q)c=\alpha[1]q'$. The last equality uses the specified shift isomorphism, rather than identifying $F(B[1])$ with $F(B)[1]$ without a map.

For any completion $c$ satisfying those two equations, $(\alpha,\alpha,c)$ is a morphism of distinguished triangles in $\mathcal T'$. Its first and second components are isomorphisms by step 2. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to conclude that $c$ is an isomorphism. Step 4 supplies at least one such completion. To check the final homotopy-colimit assertion directly, put $\widetilde p=F(p)\alpha:B'\to F(H)$ and $\widetilde q=(\alpha[1])^{-1}\xi_B F(q):F(H)\to B'[1]$. The triangle
$$B'\xrightarrow{1-s'}B'\xrightarrow{\widetilde p}F(H)\xrightarrow{\widetilde q}B'[1]$$
is isomorphic to the distinguished image triangle by $(\alpha,\alpha,1_{F(H)})$: the first square is step 3, the second is $\widetilde p=F(p)\alpha$, and the last is $\alpha[1]\widetilde q=\xi_B F(q)$. Here $\alpha[1]$ is invertible because applying the shift functor to the inverse of $\alpha$ gives its inverse. TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] therefore makes this displayed triangle distinguished. Its first arrow is $1-s'$, so [def-kun-truncations] says precisely that $F(H)$ is a homotopy colimit of the image sequence. No uniqueness of the third component is asserted.
